displayPattern: Amber LED on a Bryant 80% two-stage variable-speed furnace (troubleshooting guide TG-GFB80-02). Short flashes are the first digit and long flashes are the second. Code 12 is 1 short and 2 long
meaning: Blower on after power-up. The blower runs for 90 seconds if the furnace is powered up during a call for heat, or if that call opens during the blower on-delay. The same guide's sequence says the amber LED flashes 12 during those 90 seconds, then stays on continuously if no fault is found.
causes: 115 V or 24 V power returned while the furnace was in a call for heat
The call for heat opened during the blower on-delay
diySteps: Count 1 short flash and 2 long flashes before you turn the furnace off. This pattern is the 90-second blower run, not a lockout
Wait out the 90 seconds. The chart says the LED returns to continuous on when no fault is present
If a different counted code replaces 12, use that code. Do not clear history to erase 12
safetyNote: If you smell gas, do not touch any electrical switch or use a phone in the building; leave immediately and call your gas supplier from outside. Turn off electrical power at the furnace switch or breaker before opening any panel, and never bypass or jumper a limit, rollout or pressure switch. Gas valve, burner, venting, wiring and control-board work should be done by a licensed HVAC technician.
proAdvice: Call a licensed HVAC technician if the blower does not stop after the 90 seconds, or if a fault code replaces 12.
